images.title: Two scales on a protractor
images.purpose: A protractor has two scales so you can read from either arm as the 0 line.
images.composition: One large half-circle protractor outline in the middle with a lot of white space around.
images.exact_structure: One flat semicircle protractor outline in grey #6B7280 with the straight edge at the bottom and a centre dot. Only 3 numbers on each scale: the outer scale 0, 90, 180 running from right to left in teal #0072B2; the inner scale 0, 90, 180 running from left to right in amber #E69F00. No other ticks. Exactly 1 protractor, 6 numbers.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the following: more ticks than stated
images.takeaway: Two scales let you start from the 0 line on either side.
images.description: A grey protractor outline with a teal scale running 0 to 180 from the right and an amber scale running 0 to 180 from the left.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at where each scale starts at 0.

image_decisions.why: The two-scale idea is one clean picture of a protractor with two number rows.
